specification.problem: Estimate a systematic error parameter of an experimentally implemented single-qubit gate (here the over/under-rotation angle, i.e. amplitude error, of a nominal pi/2 X rotation) with Heisenberg-scaling accuracy, using only a single qubit, no entanglement, and a robust iterative phase-estimation procedure in the style of Higgins et al.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest useful construction (chosen as an assumption, since no experiment_scope was supplied): nonadaptive robust phase estimation of the rotation angle theta of a single-qubit gate G(theta)=exp(-i theta X/2), with amplitude error epsilon = theta - pi/2. Tiny explicit instance: J=3 refinement rounds with repetition numbers k_j = 2^j in {1,2,4}, two measurement bases (Z and Y) per round, M shots per circuit, true value epsilon = 0.05. Outside scope: the off-resonance (detuning) error estimation construction, the paper's explicit robustness theorem (tolerated additive error bounds on probabilities, SPAM-error tolerance), the specific shot-number schedule M_j and constant factors in the Heisenberg bound, and the full universal gate-set calibration workflow.

Implemented single-qubit gate, modeled as an ideal X rotation by angle \theta

equations.label: Gate model with amplitude error
equations.description: The implemented gate is modeled as an X rotation whose angle deviates from the nominal pi/2 by the amplitude error epsilon.
equations.justification: The abstract names amplitude errors as a target parameter but gives no gate model; this is the simplest model in which amplitude error is a single angle.
assumptions: Gate is a pure X-axis rotation (no off-resonance/detuning component in this scoped instance)
Errors are systematic and identical across repetitions

equations.label: Z-basis outcome probability after k repetitions
equations.description: Exact probability of measuring 0 in the computational basis after applying the gate k times to |0>, under the model of eq_1.
equations.justification: Direct computation from G(theta)^k = exp(-i k theta X/2) acting on |0>.
assumptions: Ideal state preparation and measurement for this exact expression; the robust procedure is designed to tolerate deviations but those bounds are not reconstructed here

equations.label: Y-basis outcome probability after k repetitions
equations.description: Exact probability of the +1 eigenvalue of Y after k gate applications; together with eq_2 this determines k theta modulo 2 pi rather than only its cosine.
equations.justification: G(theta)^k|0> = cos(k theta/2)|0> - i sin(k theta/2)|1>, whose Y expectation is -sin(k theta).
assumptions: Y-basis measurement implemented by S^dagger then H before a Z measurement, assumed ideal in this exact expression

equations.label: Phase extraction in round j
equations.description: Estimate of the accumulated phase k_j theta modulo 2 pi from the two empirical probabilities; this is an approximation whose error shrinks with the shot number M_j.
equations.abstract_quote: Our main theorem making this possible is a robust version of the phase estimation procedure of Higgins et al.
equations.justification: Higgins-style phase estimation extracts a phase from repeated applications of a unitary; with a single qubit and no ancilla the phase k theta must be read out from two complementary measurement bases, inferred from the abstract's claim of operating entirely within a single-qubit Hilbert space.
assumptions: Empirical probabilities are within an additive error of the exact values (statistical plus SPAM error); the tolerated error threshold from the paper's theorem is not reconstructed

equations.label: Iterative refinement (unwrapping) of the estimate
equations.description: Round j selects, among the k_j candidate angles consistent with the measured phase modulo 2 pi, the one closest (in circular distance) to the previous estimate; each round halves the uncertainty interval provided the previous estimate's error is below pi/(2 k_j).
equations.justification: Standard iterative (Kitaev/Higgins-type) phase estimation refinement using doubling repetition numbers; the abstract names the Higgins et al. procedure but does not state the update rule.
assumptions: Each round's phase error is below pi/2 so the correct candidate is selected

equations.label: Heisenberg scaling of the final estimate
equations.description: The error of the final estimate decreases inversely with the total number of gate applications N (counting both measurement bases), as opposed to the standard quantum limit 1/sqrt(N).
equations.abstract_quote: our estimates achieve the optimal efficiency, Heisenberg scaling, and do so without entanglement and entirely within a single-qubit Hilbert space
equations.justification: The abstract explicitly claims Heisenberg scaling; the definition of N as total gate applications and the constant factors are not given in the abstract.
assumptions: N counted as total number of gate applications across all circuits and shots
Constant prefactor and the required shot schedule M_j come from the paper's theorem and are not reconstructed

registers.name: q
registers.role: Single system qubit on which the gate under calibration is applied repeatedly and then measured

specification.initial_state: |0\rangle on the single qubit q (assumed ideal preparation; the paper's robustness to preparation error is outside the reconstructed scope)

steps.description: For each round j = 0,...,J-1 (instance J=3, k_j in {1,2,4}): prepare |0>, apply the gate under test k_j = 2^j times in sequence.
Circuit A (Z basis): measure q in the computational basis, repeat M_j shots, record empirical P_{k_j}^Z(0).
Circuit B (Y basis): after the k_j gate applications apply S^dagger then H, measure in the computational basis, repeat M_j shots, record empirical P_{k_j}^Y(+y) (outcome 0 corresponds to +y).
Classically extract the wrapped phase estimate for round j from the two empirical probabilities.

Refine the running estimate of theta by selecting the candidate consistent with the wrapped phase closest to the previous round's estimate; after the final round report theta-hat and epsilon-hat = theta-hat - pi/2.

specification.measurement: Computational-basis (Z) measurement of the single qubit in two circuit variants per round: directly (Z basis) and after S^dagger H (Y basis). Each variant is repeated M_j shots to estimate outcome probabilities.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Compute wrapped phase estimates via eq_4 for each round, unwrap iteratively via eq_5 using the doubling structure k_j = 2^j, output theta-hat_{J-1} and amplitude-error estimate epsilon-hat = theta-hat_{J-1} - pi/2 (reduced to (-pi, pi]). Instance check: with epsilon = 0.05 and ideal probabilities, round phases are k_j(pi/2 + 0.05) mod 2 pi and the unwrapping recovers theta exactly.
assumptions: No experiment_scope was supplied; the scoped construction (amplitude-error estimation of an X rotation via nonadaptive doubling robust phase estimation, J=3, epsilon=0.05) is the reconstructor's choice, not established by the abstract
Gate model is a pure X rotation with no detuning; off-resonance error estimation is not reconstructed
Doubling repetition schedule k_j = 2^j and equal shot counts M_j = M are assumed; the paper may use a different schedule
Exact probability formulas assume ideal SPAM; the paper's robustness claim concerns tolerating bounded SPAM/additive errors, whose thresholds are not reconstructed
Heisenberg scaling is taken from the abstract's claim, with N defined as total gate applications by assumption
missing_information: Exact statement of the paper's main robustness theorem (tolerated additive error on probabilities, success probability, and resulting error bound with constants)
Shot-number schedule M_j and total resource count required to achieve a target accuracy
Construction and measurement circuits for the off-resonance (detuning) error parameter
How the method handles a universal single-qubit gate set (e.g., which gates, which axes, and how parameters are combined for calibration)
Whether the procedure is adaptive or nonadaptive in the paper, and the precise candidate-selection rule used for unwrapping
